Hi Jessica — great to speak earlier. Quick follow-up to make sure we have the right numbers before I put together a hosted pricing estimate and unit economics for the use case you described (real-time insights via API for customer dashboards).

Recap of what I heard:
- Primary model: generation for short answers + embeddings for search (mixed).
- Typical response sizes: ~150–500 tokens per request (median ~220).
- Traffic pattern: steady baseline with several daily spikes during business hours.

Two quick asks so we can size cost and capacity:
1) Expected monthly token volume (rough ballpark is fine): are we looking at ~1M, 5M, 10M, or 50M+ tokens/month?
2) Peak TPS (concurrent requests): what's the highest sustained TPS during your busiest 5–15 minute windows? e.g., 5 TPS, 20 TPS, 50 TPS?

You mentioned a targeting goal of ~$/1M tokens — if you have a budget range there (e.g., $8k–$20k per 1M tokens or a target unit cost), include that and I can align recommendations (batching, rate limits, or quantized model variants) accordingly.

I can have a first-pass pricing + SLA/throughput recommendation back to you tomorrow if you confirm the two numbers above.

1) Expected monthly token volume:~ 8–12M tokens/month to start (month 1–3), with projected growth to ~25M tokens/month by Q4 if adoption goes well.

Budget / unit target: We're aiming for an effective spend roughly in the range of $12k–$18k per 1M tokens (open to guidance on tradeoffs — e.g., higher latency for lower cost).

Thanks Jessica — this is super helpful. Attached a short pricing sheet and a usage estimate CSV that shows cost sensitivity at 8M / 12M / 25M tokens and options for handling peak TPS. High level summary below so it's easy to skim.

High-level fit & recommendations:
- For your starting range (8–12M tokens/mo) with 15–20 TPS peaks: Redwood Hosted standard tier + moderate batching will likely meet your latency targets while keeping costs in check.
- If you accept slightly higher 99th latency (100–300ms higher) we can route some requests to a quantized model variant that reduces unit $/1M tokens by ~20–30%.
- To handle short spikes to 45 TPS we recommend a short burst capacity policy (auto-burst to dedicated pool) rather than reserving large baseline capacity. That keeps committed spend lower while covering the rare bursts.

Estimated unit economics (ballpark):
- Base hosted price: $14,000 per 1M tokens (includes baseline throughput & standard SLA)
- With batching + prefix caching: effective $/1M tokens can drop to $10,000–$11,000 at your expected volumes
- With quantized variant and relaxed latency: target $/1M tokens could approach $8,000 at scale

Action items / next steps:
- Jessica: confirm which of the three volume scenarios (8, 12, 25M) we should model formally.
- Alex: if you can share 1–2 sample QPS graphs and a typical request size distribution (CSV is fine) I'll add detailed TPS sizing for hosted and recommended burst policy.
- We'll follow up with a short SOW + SLA + pricing sheet for your review (I attached a draft).

Attachments:

- acme-usage-estimate-2026-02.csv
